QASHANI:94:5-7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:94:5-7/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:94:5-7/r3.claim: Desire only God’s Essence when inviting people, without reward or other motive; otherwise the caller acts from self and deviates.
QASHANI:94:5-7/r3.anchor: لا ترغب إلا إلى ذاته دون ثواب أو غرض آخر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.claim: Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ completes the preceding sūrah: 93:6’s sheltering and other favours concerned the period before and just after prophethood, while this sūrah points to blessings after Islam spread in Arabia.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r1.anchor: It begins after Sūrah al-Ḍuḥā without any prior introduction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.claim: The prior sūrah predicts a bright future; this one points to predictions already beginning to materialize and assures the Prophet that hardship yields to success if faced courageously.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r2.anchor: by making a reference to some such predictions which by then had shown clear signs to materialize, an emphatic assurance is sounded to the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.claim: The discourse proceeds from inner expansion, through the recurring law of hardship with relief, to completion of the mission and disciplined use of its success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p363/r3.anchor: Initially a reference is made to the gift of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r3.claim: The directive promises that the Prophet will complete his mission after obstacles are overcome, divine help arrives, and Makkah is reconquered.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r3.anchor: First, they bring glad tidings t o the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r4.claim: After completing the mission, the Prophet is to devote all his energy more fervently to seeking God and preparing for the final journey to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r4.anchor: he should con tinue with more fervour, and direct all his energies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r5.claim: When people asked why he labored so much in worship after his sins had been forgiven, the Prophet replied that he should be a grateful servant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r5.anchor: The Prophet (s ws) is said to have replied

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r6.claim: Sūrah al-Naṣr gives an extended treatment of this instruction after victory and people enter Islam in multitudes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p367/r6.anchor: In S ūrah al-Na ṣr, an elaborate treatment is given

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r22.claim: The Prophet should turn his desire toward his Lord in every circumstance.

QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r23.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r23.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r23.claim: Another interpretation is that after conveying the message, the Prophet should seek intercession from his Lord.
QUSHAYRI:v3p432/r23.anchor: ويقال : فإذا فرغت من تبليغ الرسالة فارغب في الشفاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r11.claim: The majority understand fārghab as a command from the simple verb raghiba: direct all desires to God alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فارغب، أمر من رغب ثلاثيا: أي اصرف وجه الرغبات إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r12.speaker: زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r12.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla transmit a reading described as an imperative from the geminated form of raghiba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p501/r12.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة: فرغت، أمر من رغب بشد الغين.

FARRA:v3p275#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p275#2/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p275#2/r7.claim: When finished with prayer, exert yourself in supplication to God and desire Him; fanṣab derives from exertion.
FARRA:v3p275#2/r7.anchor: إذا فرغت من صلاتك، فانصب إلى ربك في الدعاء وارغب. قال الفراء: فانصب من النصب.

FARRA:v3p275#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p275#2/r8.speaker: شريح
FARRA:v3p275#2/r8.claim: Seeing two men wrestling, Shurayḥ said this is not what a person with free time is meant for; he should finish an obligation and exert himself in worship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r3.speaker: طاوس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r3.claim: Tawus and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz treated al-Inshirah as part of al-Duha and recited both in one obligatory prayer unit without a division.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r3.anchor: وعن طاوس وعمر بن عبد العزيز أنهما كانا يقولان : ( ألم نشرح من سورة الضحى )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r4.claim: The author calls that practice anomalous and contrary to the community's agreement on the codex's surah divisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r4.anchor: وهذا شذوذ مخالف لما اتفقت عليه الأمة من تسوير المصحف الإمام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r5.claim: The surah recalls God's gentle care, relief of the Prophet's grief and hardship, clarification, and elevation of his standing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r5.anchor: احتوت على ذكر عناية الله تعالى لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلطف الله له وإزالة الغم والحرج عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r7.claim: It promises ease whenever hardship comes, urging the Prophet to endure the mission's burdens and seek God's help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r7.anchor: واتبع ذلك بوعده بأنه كلما عرض له عسر فسيجد من أمره يسرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r6.claim: The command is to trust God and direct one's hopes to Him alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r6.anchor: أمر بالتوكل على الله تعالى وصرف وجه الرغبات إليه لا إلى سواه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r7.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads farghab with an open ra and doubled, kasra ghayn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p497#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «فرغب» بفتح الراء وشد الغين مكسورة.

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r1.speaker: زر بن حبيش
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r1.claim: He transmits a report from the Prophet saying that whoever recites Alam nashraḥ is as if they came to him while he was distressed and relieved him.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r1.anchor: وعن زر بن حبيش عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ (ألم نشرح لك صدرك)

JISHUMI:v10p7463/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r2.claim: Sūrat al-Sharḥ follows al-Ḍuḥā by recalling blessings like those just mentioned.
JISHUMI:v10p7463/r2.anchor: واتصل بسورة (والضحى) اتصال ذكر نعمة بأمثالها

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Sharḥ Makkan and place it just after Sūrah 93; Ibn ʿAbbās calls it Madinan, while some assign only vv. 5–6 to Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r1.anchor: considered by most commentators to be a Makkan sūrah, most likely revealed immediately after the preceding one. Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that it is Madinan

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.claim: Some say Sūrahs 93 and 94 were originally one, since Companions recited them together in one prayer cycle without a basmalah separating them.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.anchor: the Companions of the Prophet would recite them together in a single prayer cycle

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.claim: Ash-Sharh was revealed almost immediately after Ad-Duha and appears to continue it directly.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r1.anchor: revealed almost immediately af ter the preceding one, appears to be a direct continuation of the latter

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.speaker: Ta'us ibn Kaysan and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.claim: They regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah and recited them in prayer without a second basmala; Asad cites Razi.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r2.anchor: Ta'us ibn Kaysan, or the Caliph Umar i bn Abd al-Aziz (known as "the Second Umar") - regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah

ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.claim: The surah addresses the Prophet first and, through him, every true follower of the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:94:intro/r3.anchor: addressed in the first instance to the Prophet and, through him, to every true follower of the Qur'an

THALABI:v10p236/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p236/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p236/r5.claim: The Prophet should direct his desire to his Lord in every circumstance and toward no one else.
THALABI:v10p236/r5.anchor: وإلى ربك فارغب في جميع أحوالك [لا] إلى سواه

THALABI:v10p236/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p236/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p236/r6.claim: When free of worldly occupations, one should empty the heart for concerns of the afterlife.
THALABI:v10p236/r6.anchor: وقيل: إذا فرغت من أشغال الدنيا، ففرغ قلبك لهموم العقبى

THALABI:v10p236/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p236/r7.speaker: جعفر
THALABI:v10p236/r7.claim: Remember the Lord when free of everything besides Him.
THALABI:v10p236/r7.anchor: عن جعفر: اذكر ربك على فراغ منك عن كل ما دونه

THALABI:v10p236/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p236/r8.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p236/r8.claim: After worship, exert yourself in turning away from it for fear it may be rejected; desire God and seek forgiveness for your deed in shame.
THALABI:v10p236/r8.anchor: وقيل: إذا فرغت من العبادة، فانصب إلى الإعراض عنها مخافة ردها عليك

THALABI:v10p236/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p236/r9.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p236/r9.claim: A recitation practice transmitted through Ubayy is to pronounce takbir at the end of each surah beginning with al-Duha; the Prophet instructed Ubayy to do so.
THALABI:v10p236/r9.anchor: أخبره أبي بن كعب أنه قرأ على النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله) ، فأمره بذلك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:5/r6.claim: In work and worship, one should turn to God alone, seek His approval first, and ask only Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:94:5/r6.anchor: gerek çalışmasında gerekse ibadetinde yalnız Allah’a yönelmesi, her işini öncelikle O’nun rızasını gözeterek yapması, ne diliyorsa O’ndan dilemesi

BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r2.claim: رغب فيه or إليه means desiring and earnestly seeking it, while رغب عنه means turning away; the verse means ask God alone, since only He can help.
BURSEVI:v10p357#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى فارغب بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره فإنه القادر على إسعافك لا غيره

SULAMI:v2p405#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r1.claim: God will give the Prophet what brings joy to his eyes concerning his community.
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ليعطيك في أمتك ما تقر به عينك

SULAMI:v2p405#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r2.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r2.claim: One's desire should be directed in God and toward Him.
SULAMI:v2p405#3/r2.anchor: قال القاسم : تكون رغبتك فيه وإليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says when one finishes prayer, one should exert oneself in supplication, asking God and turning to Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فاذا فرغت فانصب الاية قال : اذا فرغت من الصلاة فانصب في الدعاء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Masud's view that completing bowing and prostration permits a person to make a request while still seated.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال : كان ابن مسعود يقول : ايما رجل احدث في اخر صلاته فقد تمت صلاته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says after finishing one's own affairs, one should pray to God and direct one's desire toward Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3446#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : فاذا فرغت فانصب قال : اذا فرغت من اسباب نفسك فصل إلى ربك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r2.claim: Here ilā is used because irghab includes turning toward someone who has one's need, like a traveler heading to his destination; compare Abraham's statement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r2.anchor: وأما تعدية فعل { فارغب } هنا بحرف { إلى } فلتضمينه معنى الإقبال والتوجه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r3.claim: Putting 'to your Lord' first makes desire exclusive to God, fitting the Messenger's supreme status; the omitted object encompasses all his aims, especially spiritual perfection, the spread of religion, and Muslim victory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r3.anchor: وتقديم إلى { ربك } على { فارغب } لإفادة الاختصاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r4.claim: The fā in fansab and farghab links the actions because fronted complements imply restriction and hence a conditional sense; Qur'anic examples show this pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r4.anchor: واعلم أن الفاء في قوله : { فانصب } ( الشرح : 7 ) وقوله : { فارغب } رابطة للفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r5.speaker: محمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r5.claim: When a man asked to join jihad, the Prophet asked whether his parents were alive and told him to strive by serving them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r5.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن سأل منه أن يخرج للجهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r6.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r6.claim: Al-Tibi cites Ibn al-Shajari's puzzlement that waw and fā meet here, since fā ordinarily marks coordination, an answer, or a relative clause; Ibn Ashur says his analysis removes the puzzle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p417/r6.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن ( أمالي السيد ) ( يعني ابن الشجري ) أن اجتماع الفاء والواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p167/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p167/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p167/r1.claim: Direct all hope and desire to God alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p167/r1.anchor: اجعل رغبتك إلى الله عز وجل وحده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r1.claim: After worldly affairs and their attachments end, one should turn energetically to worship with an unoccupied mind and sincere intention and longing for God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فإذا فرغت فانصب وإلى ربك فارغب} أي: إذا فرغت من أمور الدنيا وأشغالها وقطعت علائقها، فانصب في العبادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Dahhak say that after finishing jihad one should devote oneself to worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r7.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم، والضحاك: {فإذا فرغت} أي: من الجهاد {فانصب} أي: في العبادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r8.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r8.claim: Al-Thawri says to make one's intention and desire directed to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p433/r8.anchor: قال الثوري: اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله، عز وجل.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p777#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p777#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p777#2/r8.claim: Direct your desire solely to God, ask only His bounty, and rely on Him; another reading means urge people to seek what He has.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p777#2/r8.anchor: واجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ، ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r6.claim: He says to direct one's desire to God in supplication.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r7.claim: Another meaning is to seek His assistance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r8.claim: He says to direct oneself to God with sincerity of intention.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p298/r9.claim: A further possibility is to seek God's help in victory over enemies.

MUJAHID:v2p768#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p768#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p768#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says that after finishing worldly business and standing to pray, one should direct desire and intention to God.
MUJAHID:v2p768#2/r1.anchor: عن منصور عن مجاهد قال يقول إذا فرغت من أمر الدنيا فقمت إلى الصلاة فاجعل رغبتك ونيتك إلى الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347/r1.claim: Direct all desire specifically to the Lord, ask no one but His favor, and rely on Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347/r1.anchor: واجعل وغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل الا فضله متوكلا عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8/r14.claim: Another reading is farghab, meaning to encourage people toward what God has.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8/r14.anchor: وقرىء «فرغب» أي فرغب الناس إلى ما عنده.

QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8#2/r1.claim: Constant, uninterrupted work is not required; sustained application is disliked for ordinary people.
QURTUBI-FULL:94:7-8#2/r1.anchor: وليس يلزم الدؤوب على العمل، بل هو مكروه للخلق.

QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r1.claim: The Prophet should seek God alone, free even from concern for the people he serves through his mission; God is the provision and equipment for the hard road and struggle.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r1.anchor: إلى ربك وحده خاليا من كل شيء حتى من أمر الناس الذين تشتغل بدعوتهم

QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r2.claim: The sura closes like al-Duha with both tenderness toward the Prophet's burdens and awareness of God's affectionate care; the mission is heavy yet a channel for divine light and connection with the enduring.
QUTB-ZILAL:94:8/r2.anchor: الشعور بعظمة الود الحبيب الجليل الذي ينسم على روح الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r1.claim: One interpretation is to direct desire exclusively to God, seek only His favor, and rely on Him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r1.anchor: اجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r2.claim: Alternatively, seek from God everything desired in religion and worldly life, including victory over enemies; a variant reading means urging people to seek what God has.
RAZI-FULL:v32p8/r2.anchor: ارغب في سائر ما تلتمسه دينا ودنيا ونصرة على الأعداء إلى ربك

SAMIN-DURR:94:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:94:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:94:8/r1.claim: Farghab derives from desire; Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read faraghghib, commanding people to seek what God has.
SAMIN-DURR:94:8/r1.anchor: من الرغبة وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة " فرغب " بتشديد العين

STUDYQURAN:94:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r1.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r1.claim: The command means not to desire this world and to direct desire to God alone.
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r1.anchor: This verse is understood to mean, “Do not desire this world—let your desire be for God alone”

STUDYQURAN:94:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r2.claim: The verse exhorts prayer and insists that prayer and good deeds be directed only to please God.
STUDYQURAN:94:8/r2.anchor: On the one hand, this is an exhortation to prayer; on the other, it is an exhortation to pray only to God

TAB-FULL:v24p500/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r1.claim: Muḥammad should direct his desire and requests to his Lord alone, since his polytheist people turn to idols and rivals.
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وإلى ربك فارغب} [الشرح: 8] قال: اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله

TAB-FULL:v24p500/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r2.claim: Mujāhid says to direct one's intention and desire to God.
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وإلى ربك فارغب} [الشرح: 8] قال: اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله

TAB-FULL:v24p500/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r3.claim: In another report Mujāhid interprets the phrase as referring to standing for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p500/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإلى ربك فارغب} [الشرح: 8] قال: إذا قمت إلى الصلاة

ZAJJAJ:v5p341#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p341#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p341#2/r1.claim: Direct all longing and desire to God alone.
ZAJJAJ:v5p341#2/r1.anchor: أي اجعل رغبتك إلى الله وحده

TABRISI:94:7-8/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:94:7-8/r13.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:94:7-8/r13.claim: Desire God while fearing Hell and hoping for Paradise.
TABRISI:94:7-8/r13.anchor: يريد تضرع إليه راهبا من النار وراغبا إلى الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r1.claim: Turn your desire and intention toward your Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r1.anchor: (قوله تعالى) (¬5): {وإلى ربك فارغب} اجعل رغبتك إلى ربك ونيتك له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r2.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r2.claim: When finished with the obligatory prayers, devote yourself to night prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الله: إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r4.claim: After finishing the fight against the enemy, devote yourself to worship and direct your hopes to God; Zayd ibn Aslam agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬3)، وزيد بن أسلم (¬4): إذا فرغت من جهاد العدو فانصب في عبادة ربك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r5.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, call humbly to God in fear of the Fire and hope for Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r5.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد تضرع إليه راهبا من النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r6.claim: Direct your desire exclusively to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p137/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي اجعل رغبتك إلى الله وحده (¬2)

ELMALILI:94:7-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r4.claim: The fronted phrase “to your Lord” marks exclusivity: hope only in God and direct all effort continually toward Him.
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r4.anchor: Takdim, kasr içindir. Yani ve ancak Rabbine

ELMALILI:94:7-8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r5.claim: Do not stop at secondary causes or proximate goals; recognize the Benefactor behind each gift and work for Him, since all favor belongs to Him and He is the ultimate aim.
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r5.anchor: nimete ve esere rağbet ile kalmamalı, nimetten mün‘imi görüp hep O’na doğru yürümeli, O’nun için çalışmalıdır. Gāye-i murad O’dur

ELMALILI:94:7-8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r8.claim: These surahs move from the Prophet's condition to broader believers' destiny, passing from blessing to its Giver before al-Tin affirms the afterlife and religion.
ELMALILI:94:7-8/r8.anchor: ferdin hâlinden nev‘in hâline ve mü’minlerin âkıbetinin de güzelliğine geçilerek bu iki sûrenin bir bağlanışı

CORPUSCORANICUM:94:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: For rabb as a divine title, consult 95:8; closing worship calls also occur at 96:19 and 69:52, while 93:11 calls for proclaiming the Lord’s grace and 68:32 has comparable diction.
CORPUSCORANICUM:94:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Schlussrufe mit Aufforderung zum Gottesdienst enthalten auch 96:19 und 69:52

ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r1.claim: The Prophet should direct his desire and supplication to his Lord alone, since only God can provide assistance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r1.anchor: وإلى ربك وحده فارغب فاحرص بالسؤال ولا تسألأ غيره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r15.speaker: زيد بن علي، ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r15.claim: Zayd ibn Ali and Ibn Abi Abla read فرغب as an imperative with doubled ghayn, meaning invite people to seek what God has.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p172/r15.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة فرغب أمر من رغب بشد الغين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r1.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r1.claim: A person should implore God, fearing Hell and hoping for Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r1.anchor: قال عطاء: تضرع إليه راهبا من النار راغبا في الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r2.claim: Another view takes the command as seeking God in every circumstance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r2.anchor: وقيل: فارغب إليه في جميع أحوالك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says to direct one's desire to God alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p467/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: 196/أأي اجعل رغبتك إلى الله وحده.

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r2.claim: The Prophet should direct his hope and requests to God alone, who alone can help him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r2.anchor: بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره فإنه القادر وحده على إسعافك

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r3.claim: A reading in the passive sense means “make people desire” God's reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r3.anchor: وقرىء «فرغب» أي فرغب الناس إلى طلب ثوابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.claim: A report likens reciting this sura to visiting the Prophet while distressed and relieving him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:94:7-8/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة ألم نشرح فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتم ففرج عني

BINTSHATI:v1p75/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p75/r2.claim: If finishing must be specified, it is the release from confusion, distress, and constriction; once relieved, Muhammad should devote himself to the burdens and struggle of his message.
BINTSHATI:v1p75/r2.anchor: هو فراغ اليسر بعد العسر، والراحة النفسية بعد الشدة والكرب، فلينصب المصطفى لتكاليف رسالته

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r1.claim: In Quranic usage outside religious contexts, raghaba denotes strong inclination.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r1.anchor: وجاءت في غير السياق الديني، بمعنى الميل القوي.

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r2.claim: In this construction, fronting ila rabbika makes the desire exclusive to God.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r2.anchor: وهو أسلوب بلاغي يفيد القصر والتخصيص

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r3.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says Muhammad should direct his hopes for every need to God alone, unlike his idolatrous opponents.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r3.anchor: أجعل رغبتك إلى ربك دون من سواه من خلقه

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r4.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r4.claim: Al-Nishaburi says Muhammad should hope in his Lord, not another, for what he longs for and the good of both worlds.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r4.anchor: وأرغب إلى ربك في إنجاز المأمول لا إلى غيره

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r5.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r5.claim: Abduh says one should seek recompense for one's deeds from God alone.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r5.anchor: لا ترغب إلى أحد في استثمار أعمالك إلا إلى الله وحده

BINTSHATI:v1p76/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r6.claim: The conjunction ties the exclusive desire for God to the preceding relief and promises, completing the surah's unified movement from distress to ease.
BINTSHATI:v1p76/r6.anchor: ووصل الآية بما قبلها، هو الذي يطرد به النسق وتتم وحدة السياق في السورة كلها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r6.claim: The servant should direct hope and petition to the Lord alone, since He alone has power and gives creatures whatever power they possess.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r6.anchor: أي بالسؤال لأنه القادر وحده كما قدر على تربيتك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r9.claim: Aspiring to the better hereafter also hints at the approaching end of life, as signaled by Sūrat al-Naṣr.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p466/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى قرب الأجل بما أشارت إليه سورة النصر

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r1.claim: When finished with prayer and tashahhud, the Prophet is to turn to God and ask for his need.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فإذا فرغت فانصب} الآية قال: قال الله لرسوله: إذا فرغت من صلاتك وتشهدت

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r2.claim: He interprets finishing as turning to supplication and seeking one's requests from God.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {فإذا فرغت فانصب} إلى الدعاء {وإلى ربك فارغب} في المسألة

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r3.claim: Another report says finishing the bowing and prostrations completes prayer; one may make requests while seated.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كان ابن مسعود يقول: أيما رجل أحدث في آخر صلاته فقد تمت صلاته

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r5.claim: He says that after sitting, one should strive in supplication and asking.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد {فإذا فرغت فانصب} قال: إذا جلست فاجتهد في الدعاء والمسألة

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r6.claim: Another explanation says that after finishing personal affairs, one should pray and direct one's desire to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فإذا فرغت فانصب} قال: إذا فرغت من أسباب نفسك فصل {وإلى ربك فارغب}

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r7.claim: He says that after prayer the Prophet should devote himself to supplication and desire God in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {فإذا فرغت فانصب} قال: إذا فرغت من صلاتك فانصب في الدعاء

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r8.claim: He takes finishing to mean the obligatory prayer and turning to God in requests and supplication.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك {فإذا فرغت} قال: من الصلاة المكتوبة {وإلى ربك فارغب} قال: في المسألة والدعاء

DURR-FULL:v8p551/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says that when the Prophet finishes a military expedition he should work hard in worship.
DURR-FULL:v8p551/r9.anchor: قال الحسن: أمره إذا فرغ من غزوه أن يجتهد في العبادة

ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r1.claim: The majority reading is an imperative from the basic triliteral verb: direct all desires to God alone, never to another.
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فارغب } ،   أمر من رغب ثلاثياً

ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAblah read the form with a doubled ghayn.
ABUHAYYAN:94:8/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة : فرغت ،   أمر من رغب

ALUSI:94:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:8/r1.claim: Direct longing and requests to the Lord alone, asking no one else, since He alone can grant what is sought.
ALUSI:94:8/r1.anchor: فاحرص بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره تعالى فإنه القادر على الاسعاف

BAGHAWI:94:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:8/r1.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:94:8/r1.claim: ʿAta says to implore God, fearing the Fire and desiring Paradise.
BAGHAWI:94:8/r1.anchor: قال عطاء : تضرع إليه راهباً من النار راغباً في الجنة

BAGHAWI:94:8/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:94:8/r2.claim: Another view is that one should direct desire toward God in every circumstance.
BAGHAWI:94:8/r2.anchor: وقيل : فارغب إليه في جميع أحوالك

BAGHAWI:94:8/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:8/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:94:8/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says to make one's desire belong to God alone.
BAGHAWI:94:8/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : أي اجعل رغبتك إلى الله وحده

BAYDAWI:94:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:8/r1.claim: Ask your Lord and no one else, because He alone can grant your request.
BAYDAWI:94:8/r1.anchor: وإلى ربك فارغب بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره فإنه القادر وحده على إسعافك

BAYDAWI:94:8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:8/r2.claim: A variant reading has faraghib, meaning “make people desire His reward.”
BAYDAWI:94:8/r2.anchor: وقرئ فرغب أي فرغب الناس إلى طلب ثوابه

BAYDAWI:94:8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:8/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:94:8/r3.claim: A closing report says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Sharḥ is as if he came to the Prophet distressed and relieved him.
BAYDAWI:94:8/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : من قرأ سورة ( ألم نشرح ) فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتم ففرج عني .

BIQAI:94:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r1.claim: The Lord addressed is the one who bestowed the favors described in these two sūras in particular.
BIQAI:94:8/r1.anchor: أي المحسن إليك بما ذكر في هاتين السورتين خاصة

BIQAI:94:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r2.claim: Direct your requests to God, since He alone has power and alone nurtured the Prophet in the past; the servant should yearn for Him in every state.
BIQAI:94:8/r2.anchor: أي بالسؤال لأنه القادر وحده كما قدر على تربيتك فيما مضى وحده

BIQAI:94:8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r3.claim: The yearning toward God is the servant’s constant mark in every condition.
BIQAI:94:8/r3.anchor: والرغب شعار العبد دائماً في كل حال

BIQAI:94:8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r4.claim: The sūra’s ending joins back to its opening as effect to cause, and also fits what follows in the Qurʾānic sequence.
BIQAI:94:8/r4.anchor: فقد اتصل هذا الآخر بالأول اتصال المعلول بالعلة ، ولاءم ما بعدها بذلك أيضاً بعينه ملاءمة الشمس بالأهلة

BIQAI:94:8/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r5.claim: Biqāʿī reads the ending as an exhortation to intensified worship after the jihad against disbelievers in Arabia ended eight years after the Hijra, seeking the better afterlife.
BIQAI:94:8/r5.anchor: وآخر هذه السورة مشير إلى الاجتهاد في العبادة عند الفراغ من جهاد الكفار في جزيرة العرب

BIQAI:94:8/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:8/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:8/r6.claim: He takes the wish for the afterlife as a sign that the Prophet’s death was near, as indicated by Sūrat al-Naṣr.
BIQAI:94:8/r6.anchor: رغبة في الأخرى التي هي خير من الأولى ، إشارة إلى قرب الأجل بما أشارت إليه سورة النصر

DURR:94:7/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:7/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:94:7/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud glosses exertion as supplication and turning to the Lord as asking.
DURR:94:7/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود { فإذا فرغت فانصب } إلى الدعاء { وإلى ربك فارغب } في المسألة

DURR:94:7/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:7/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:94:7/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Mas'ud's view that a person's prayer is complete if ritual impurity occurs at its end; finishing means after bowing and prostration, then asking God while seated.
DURR:94:7/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك قال : كان ابن مسعود يقول : أيما رجل أحدث في آخر صلاته ، فقد تمت صلاته

DURR:94:7/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:7/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:7/r7.claim: Mujahid says that after one's personal affairs are finished, one should pray and make one's desire solely toward the Lord.
DURR:94:7/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { فإذا فرغت فانصب } قال : إذا فرغت من أسباب نفسك فصل { وإلى ربك فارغب }

DURR:94:7/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:7/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:94:7/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse means to finish the obligatory prayer and then turn to God with requests and supplication.
DURR:94:7/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك { فإذا فرغت } قال : من الصلاة المكتوبة { وإلى ربك فارغب } قال : في المسألة والدعاء

DURR:94:7/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:7/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR:94:7/r10.claim: Qatada says that after prayer the Prophet was commanded to turn to God in supplication; al-Hasan instead says after a campaign he should strive in worship.
DURR:94:7/r10.anchor: عن قتادة { فإذا فرغت فانصب وإلى ربك فارغب } قال : أمره إذا فرغ من الصلاة أن يرغب في الدعاء إلى ربه

DURR:94:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:8/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:94:8/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud glosses exertion as supplication and turning to the Lord as asking.
DURR:94:8/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود { فإذا فرغت فانصب } إلى الدعاء { وإلى ربك فارغب } في المسألة

DURR:94:8/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:8/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:94:8/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Mas'ud's view that a person's prayer is complete if ritual impurity occurs at its end; finishing means after bowing and prostration, then asking God while seated.
DURR:94:8/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك قال : كان ابن مسعود يقول : أيما رجل أحدث في آخر صلاته ، فقد تمت صلاته

DURR:94:8/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:8/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:8/r7.claim: Mujahid says that after one's personal affairs are finished, one should pray and make one's desire solely toward the Lord.
DURR:94:8/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { فإذا فرغت فانصب } قال : إذا فرغت من أسباب نفسك فصل { وإلى ربك فارغب }

DURR:94:8/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:8/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:94:8/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse means to finish the obligatory prayer and then turn to God with requests and supplication.
DURR:94:8/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك { فإذا فرغت } قال : من الصلاة المكتوبة { وإلى ربك فارغب } قال : في المسألة والدعاء

DURR:94:8/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:8/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR:94:8/r10.claim: Qatada says that after prayer the Prophet was commanded to turn to God in supplication; al-Hasan instead says after a campaign he should strive in worship.
DURR:94:8/r10.anchor: عن قتادة { فإذا فرغت فانصب وإلى ربك فارغب } قال : أمره إذا فرغ من الصلاة أن يرغب في الدعاء إلى ربه

IBNASHUR:94:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r1.claim: This command follows the command to thank God for His blessings and asks for their continued increase, as in 14:7.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r1.anchor: عطف على تفريع الأمر بالشكر على النعم أمر بطلب استمرار نعم الله تعالى عليه

IBNASHUR:94:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r2.claim: Raghbah is seeking the attainment of what one loves; normally the sought person takes a direct object and the desired thing is introduced by fī.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r2.anchor: طلب حصول ما هو محبوب وأصله أن يعدى إلى المطلوب منه بنفسه ويعدى إلى الشيء المطلوب ب

IBNASHUR:94:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
IBNASHUR:94:8/r3.claim: In 4:127, raghb in the construction with ʿan means turning desire away; ʿĀʾisha explains the phrase by supplying an omitted ʿan before an.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r3.anchor: وذلك تأويل عائشة أم المؤمنين كما تقدم في سورة النساء

IBNASHUR:94:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r4.claim: The verb takes ilā here because it includes the sense of turning toward or approaching, like traveling to someone who has what one needs.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r4.anchor: فلتضمينه معنى الإقبال والتوجه تشبيها بسير السائر إلى من عنده حاجته

IBNASHUR:94:8/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r5.claim: Putting “to your Lord” first restricts desire to God alone; this exclusivity befits the greatest quality of a messenger and rules out desiring another.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r5.anchor: أي إليه لا إلى غيره تكون رغبتك فإن صفة الرسالة أعظم صفات الخلق

IBNASHUR:94:8/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r6.claim: The object of “desire” is omitted to encompass everything the Prophet might seek: spiritual perfection, the spread of religion, and victory for Muslims.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r6.anchor: ليعم كل ما يرغبه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهل يرغب النبي إلا في الكمال النفساني وانتشار الدين ونصر المسلمين

IBNASHUR:94:8/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r7.claim: The fāʾ links the verbs because fronting their complements implies restriction and thereby a conditional sense; this is common, as in the cited verses.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r7.anchor: رابطة للفعل لأن تقديم المعمول يتضمن معنى الاشتراط والتقييد فإن تقديم المعمول لما أفاد الاختصاص نشأ منه معنى الاشتراط

IBNASHUR:94:8/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:94:8/r8.claim: When a man asked to go out for jihad, the Prophet asked whether he had parents and told him to strive in their service; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites this as a preposed phrase treated conditionally.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r8.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن سأل منه أن يخرج للجهاد

IBNASHUR:94:8/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r9.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR:94:8/r9.claim: Al-Ṭībī, citing al-Sayyid’s A Amālī (Ibn al-Shajarī), calls the combination of fāʾ and wāw here one of the most astonishing expressions because fāʾ has other usual syntactic roles.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r9.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن « أمالي السيد » ( يعني ابن الشجري ) أن اجتماع الفاء والواو هنا من أعجب كلامهم

IBNASHUR:94:8/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:8/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:8/r10.claim: Once the restrictive force of the fronted complement is understood as conditional, there is no reason for al-Ṭībī’s puzzlement about the fāʾ and wāw.
IBNASHUR:94:8/r10.anchor: ولا يبقى تعجب بعد ما قررناه

IBNATIYYA:94:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:8/r1.claim: The verse commands reliance on God and directing every desire to Him alone.
IBNATIYYA:94:8/r1.anchor: أمر بالتوكل على الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA:94:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:8/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA:94:8/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads farghab with fatḥa on the rāʾ and a doubled ghayn bearing kasra.

IBNKATHIR:94:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r1.claim: When worldly duties are finished and their distractions set aside, devote yourself energetically and wholeheartedly to worship, with sincere intention and desire directed to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r1.anchor: أي : إذا فرغت من أمور الدنيا وأشغالها وقطعت علائقها ، فانصب في العبادة ، وقم إليها نشيطا فارغ البال ، وأخلص لربك النية والرغبة .

IBNKATHIR:94:7/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Masʿūd says to turn to one's Lord after finishing prayer, while still seated.
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r7.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن مسعود : { فَانْصَبْ وَإِلَى رَبِّكَ فَارْغَبْ } بعد فراغك من الصلاة وأنت جالس .

IBNKATHIR:94:7/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم والضحاك
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say that after jihad one should devote oneself to worship and turn one's desire to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r9.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم ، والضحاك : { فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ } أي : من الجهاد { فَانْصَبْ } أي : في العبادة .

IBNKATHIR:94:7/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r10.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r10.claim: Al-Thawrī says to direct one's intention and desire to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:7/r10.anchor: قال الثوري : اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله ، عز وجل .

IBNKATHIR:94:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r1.claim: When worldly duties are finished and their distractions set aside, devote yourself energetically and wholeheartedly to worship, with sincere intention and desire directed to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r1.anchor: أي : إذا فرغت من أمور الدنيا وأشغالها وقطعت علائقها ، فانصب في العبادة ، وقم إليها نشيطا فارغ البال ، وأخلص لربك النية والرغبة .

IBNKATHIR:94:8/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Masʿūd says to turn to one's Lord after finishing prayer, while still seated.
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r7.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن مسعود : { فَانْصَبْ وَإِلَى رَبِّكَ فَارْغَبْ } بعد فراغك من الصلاة وأنت جالس .

IBNKATHIR:94:8/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم والضحاك
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say that after jihad one should devote oneself to worship and turn one's desire to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r9.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم ، والضحاك : { فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ } أي : من الجهاد { فَانْصَبْ } أي : في العبادة .

IBNKATHIR:94:8/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r10.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r10.claim: Al-Thawrī says to direct one's intention and desire to God.
IBNKATHIR:94:8/r10.anchor: قال الثوري : اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله ، عز وجل .

KASHSHAF:94:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:94:8/r1.claim: Direct desire especially to the Lord, ask only for His favor, and rely on Him.
KASHSHAF:94:8/r1.anchor: واجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصاً ، ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلاً عليه .

KASHSHAF:94:8/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:8/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:94:8/r2.claim: An alternate reading has “farghiba,” meaning that the Prophet should direct people to seek what God has.
KASHSHAF:94:8/r2.anchor: وقرىء : «فرغب » أي : رغب الناس إلى طلب ما عنده .

KASHSHAF:94:8/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:94:8/r3.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:94:8/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Sharḥ is as if they came to him while he was distressed and relieved him.
KASHSHAF:94:8/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " من قرأ ألم نشرح ، فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتمّ ففرج عني " .

MAWARDI:94:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:8/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:94:8/r1.claim: The Prophet should turn to God in supplication.
MAWARDI:94:8/r1.anchor: أحدها : فارغب إليه في دعائك قاله ابن مسعود

MAWARDI:94:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:8/r2.claim: The Prophet should seek God’s help.

MAWARDI:94:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:8/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:94:8/r3.claim: The Prophet should seek God with sincerity of intention.
MAWARDI:94:8/r3.anchor: الثالث : في إخلاص نيتك ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:94:8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:8/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:8/r4.claim: A further possibility is that the Prophet should seek God’s help in victory over his enemies.
MAWARDI:94:8/r4.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : فارغب إليه في نصرك على أعدائك

NASAFI:94:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:8/r1.claim: Direct all desire to the Lord alone, ask only His favor, and rely on Him.
NASAFI:94:8/r1.anchor: واجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصاً ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلاً عليه

NASAFI:94:8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:8/r2.claim: Nasafi connects reliance on God with 14:11.

QURTUBI:94:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:8/r1.claim: A variant reads farghiba, meaning urge people to desire what is with God.
QURTUBI:94:8/r1.anchor: أي فرغب الناس إلى ما عنده .

QURTUBI:94:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:8/r2.speaker: شريح
QURTUBI:94:8/r2.claim: Shurayh rebuked people playing on Eid, saying the lawgiver had not commanded it; Ibn al-Arabi questions this judgment.
QURTUBI:94:8/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي : روي عن شريح أنه مر بقوم يلعبون يوم عيد ، فقال : ما بهذا أمر الشارع . وفيه نظر

QURTUBI:94:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:8/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi counters that Abyssinians played with shields and spears in the mosque on Eid while the Prophet watched.
QURTUBI:94:8/r3.anchor: فإن الحبش كانوا يلعبون بالدرق والحراب في المسجد يوم العيد ، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينظر .

QURTUBI:94:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:94:8/r4.claim: When Abu Bakr objected to two Ansari girls singing at Aisha's home, the Prophet told him to leave them because it was Eid.
QURTUBI:94:8/r4.anchor: ودخل أبو بكر في بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على عائشة رضي الله عنها وعندها جاريتان من جواري الأنصار تغنيان

QURTUBI:94:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:8/r5.claim: Constant, uninterrupted work is not obligatory; Qurtubi says it is disliked for human beings.
QURTUBI:94:8/r5.anchor: وليس يلزم الدؤوب على العمل ، بل هو مكروه للخلق .

RAZI:94:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:94:8/r1.claim: One interpretation is to direct one's desire exclusively to God, ask only His favor, and rely on Him.
RAZI:94:8/r1.anchor: اجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

RAZI:94:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:94:8/r2.claim: A second interpretation is to seek from God all religious and worldly needs, including victory over enemies.
RAZI:94:8/r2.anchor: ارغب في سائر ما نلتمسه دينا ودنيا ونصرة على الأعداء إلى ربك

RAZI:94:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:94:8/r3.claim: A variant reading, farghab, makes the command mean to encourage people to seek what God has.
RAZI:94:8/r3.anchor: وقرئ فرغب أي رغب الناس إلى طلب ما عنده

TAB:94:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:7/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:94:7/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd transmits from his father that after the jihad against the Arabs ended, the Prophet should turn to worship and desire his Lord.
TAB:94:7/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  فَإذَا فَرَغْتَ فانْصَبْ قال عن أبيه :  فإذا فرغت من الجهاد

TAB:94:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:94:8/r1.claim: The Prophet should direct his longing to his Lord alone, since his polytheist people direct their requests to idols and rival gods.
TAB:94:8/r1.anchor: وإلى ربك يا محمد فاجعل رغبتك ،   دون من سواه من خلقه ،   إذ كان هؤلاء المشركون

TAB:94:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:8/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:8/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the command as directing one’s intention and desire to God.
TAB:94:8/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد وَإلى رَبّكَ فارْغَبْ قال :  اجعل نيتك ورغبتك إلى الله .

TAB:94:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:8/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:8/r3.claim: Mujahid also glosses the phrase as applying when one rises to pray.
TAB:94:8/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  وَإلى رَبّكَ فارْغَبْ قال :  إذا قمت إلى الصلاة .
